# zkp_req response conformance vectors

One JSON file per case. These are the shared conformance file for every
implementation that validates a `zkp_req` presentation (Rust here, as
`zkp_req_response::validate_response`; the Kotlin and Swift SDKs may reuse them
verbatim). Files named `ok_*` must be accepted; `err_*` must be refused with the
stated reason code. The normative text is
[`docs/zkp_req_response.md`](../../../../../docs/zkp_req_response.md).

The set is generated by `scripts/gen_zkp_req_response_vectors.py` (hand-rolled
CBOR, deterministic; run it to regenerate, never edit a file by hand).

```json
{
  "description": "what the case shows",
  "query": { },                 // the Credential Query the response answers (as in ../zkp_req)
  "client_metadata": { },       // the request's client_metadata ({} offers nothing)
  "vp_token": { },              // the vp_token object; each presentation is base64url(CBOR)
  "vp_token_text": "{not json", // instead of `vp_token`: raw text (unparseable input, duplicate members)
  "expect": { "valid": true }   // or { "error": "<code>" }
}
```

Exactly one of `vp_token` / `vp_token_text`. `query` and `client_metadata` are
the request-side inputs of the planner; every vector's request must plan.

`vp_token` carries the presentations as unpadded base64url strings; decode them
to read the CBOR. Vectors that need malformed CBOR (indefinite lengths,
trailing bytes, truncation, duplicate keys) carry the raw bytes the same way.

## `expect.error`

A stable code, not message text. The first rule broken is reported, in the
order given in the spec's "Order of checks":

`response_not_parseable`, `duplicate_member`, `query_id_missing`,
`presentations_not_array`, `presentations_empty`,
`presentations_multiple_not_allowed`, `presentation_not_string`,
`presentation_not_base64url`, `cbor_malformed`, `cbor_indefinite_length`,
`cbor_trailing_bytes`, `cbor_duplicate_key`, `presentation_not_map`,
`presentation_key_not_text`, `presentation_unknown_member`,
`presentation_member_missing`, `presentation_member_wrong_type`,
`system_id_not_offered`, `proof_empty`, `issuer_key_set_empty`,
`issuer_key_set_too_many`, `issuer_key_not_bytes`, `issuer_key_empty`,
`issuer_key_too_large`, `proof_time_missing`, `proof_time_not_tdate`,
`proof_time_form`, `result_key_not_text`, `result_handle_unexpected`,
`result_handle_missing`, `result_function_unknown`, `result_wrong_type`,
`result_not_satisfied`, `pseudonym_prf_unknown`, `pseudonym_wrong_length`.

## Scope

Structure and the request/response binding only. The proof is not verified;
`issuer_key_set` is checked for limits (8 elements, 4096 bytes each),
certificates are not parsed. The `proof_time` tolerance check is the verifier's
(`proof_time::check_tolerance`, vectors in `../proof_time/`). No vector depends
on how `verifier_input` is formed: results are opaque bytes of the right
length.
